rationale: A is more useful because it gives a concrete recommendation, defines a measurable accuracy KPI, and includes at least some quantitative tradeoff evidence on error versus runtime. Its weaknesses are poor explicit comparison to alternatives and missing revisit triggers. B has a sensible general idea—target complexity where it matters—but it does not clearly name a chosen option, lacks quantitative support, and gives weaker discrimination among live alternatives. For a careful decision-maker choosing model parameters under an accuracy-versus-burden tradeoff, A provides more actionable and testable guidance.
